text.tspan: MIRAI — one feature from request to live (design v5, approved)
Every document: author agent -> script lint -> separate verifier agent -> YOU approve. Every ticket: a plain script runs the loop with round caps. Agents never merge, never deploy to production.
2 · Design (full track, or an ADR-worthy decision; otherwise straight to 3)
4 · Per ticket — supervised or overnight (orchestrator: a plain script, not an agent)
re-plan · retry · drop, with your note)
cap 2 rounds (3 high risk) · budget in turns/tokens/min

Env faults (stack down, flaky test, API error) never use a round: preflight, re-run once, circuit breaker stops the night. Stacked child: when the parent changes it waits; when the parent merges, MIRAI rebases it (--onto) and re-checks; same code hash = review still counts.
5 · Merge and go live (release mode is chosen per epic)
B) release: together (whole epic at once)
Safety under every agent run: OS sandbox, no escape · deny rules: nothing outside the project, no commit/push, no gh/docker/claude/mirai · hooks block secrets
tests only through the MIRAI MCP broker in hardened containers · pre-push + CI secret scan · only the orchestrator commits and pushes · red-team suite green before any headless run
Logged under every step: orchestrator store (run progress, rounds, budgets, reviews, QA; 90-day retention, mirai clean) + signed records on the branch -> trust metrics
+ mirai feedback <ticket> "<text>" and the reason on every edit/reject -> MIRAI suggests which gates can move to auto; it never flips one itself
